name: Noida International Airport, Jewar
description: Airport runway and terminal construction replacing agricultural fields; public environmental clearance on record. Registered platform boundary is approximate.

replay.note: Expected from the inspected pair: activity matching a registered zone. The pair brackets multi-year construction, not a single-day event. Nearby fields also change with crops. Only construction inside the illustrative registered platform should match the zone; the document does not establish compliance with every condition.

name: Navi Mumbai International Airport, Ulwe
description: Runway and terminal built on an already graded airport platform between 2021 and 2025. Public EC/CRZ records exist; the registered platform outline is illustrative.

sources.title: NMIA Environmental & CRZ compliance report, April–September 2025

replay.note: Expected from the inspected pair: activity matching a registered zone. This pair demonstrates building on prepared land, not the original hill removal or mangrove reclamation. Wetland changes outside the airport platform must be judged separately. The old and renewed clearance have separate registry periods.

name: Parsa East Kete Basan mine, Hasdeo Arand
description: Open-cast mine with visible bench advance and changing bare ground. Phase-II authorisation is documented; clearance and environmental concerns have been contested. Approximate mine footprint only.

sources.title: Supreme Court order, CA 4395/2014, 16 October 2023 (Indian Kanoon transcript)
NGT e-Journal 2025, pp.32–36, OA 59/2024 and connected matters

replay.note: Expected from the inspected pair: activity matching a registered zone. Authorised is a registry match, not a legal conclusion. The zone is a conservative illustrative mine footprint, not the lease or full Phase-II forest-diversion boundary. Its start date is the documented state permission of 25 March 2022, so early replay scenes before that date are not covered by this entry.

name: Rawa–Nangal border ridge quarries
description: Quarrying on the Rawa–Nangal border ridge. Public NGT filings discuss reported unauthorised workings and nearby Rajasthan leases. No authorisation on record in this system's registry; this is not evidence that every quarry lacks a permit.

sources.title: Rajasthan respondent reply in NGT OA 06/2025, incident-site coordinates
Haryana respondent reply in NGT OA 06/2025

replay.note: Expected from the inspected pair: physical change with no authorisation on record. The monitored area crosses a state boundary; imagery alone cannot place individual cuts in a state or lease. The reported encroachment is too small to attribute reliably at 10 m. Nearby Rajasthan permits are explicitly documented. Never describe all visible quarrying as unauthorised. A cross-tile 2021 candidate had visibly different alignment and was rejected; only Sentinel-2 tile 43RGL is used for the pair.

name: Mundakkai–Chooralmala debris-flow corridor, Wayanad
description: Visible widening and deposition along the 30 July 2024 debris-flow corridor. The monitored area includes the source area and part of the runout, not the entire approximately 8 km path.

sources.title: Yunus et al., Documenting the Wayanad landslide

replay.note: Expected from the inspected pair: a natural event. The checked clear dates are 5 February and 16 December 2024: the latter is a delayed optical view, not immediate disaster detection. A 5.5 km monitored area cannot contain the complete approximately 8 km runout. Do not call this Puthumala: the selected corridor is the 2024 Mundakkai–Chooralmala event, distinct from the 2019 Puthumala disaster.

name: Kanha forest–meadow seasonal reference
description: Forest–meadow mosaic showing dry-season canopy browning and post-monsoon greening. Same-season April 2023 and April 2024 imagery retain the same wooded margins; intended no-alert reference.

sources.title: Madhya Pradesh Tourism: Kanha National Park, seasonal vegetation guidance

replay.note: Expected from the inspected pair: a seasonal change with no alert. This is an interior forest–meadow mosaic, not a verified buffer cadastral polygon or a pure sal stand. No conspicuous new clearing is visible in these checked views; this is not proof that none occurred between dates. Do not infer leaf loss from NDVI alone.

name: Yamuna floodplain near Shastri Park, Delhi
description: Yamuna flooding during the documented July 2023 event; water spread is visible in clear portions of a partly cloudy 13 July scene. Cloud-limited replay: this site allows tile cloud up to 85 percent to reach that scene.

sources.title: NRSC Delhi flood report, 13 July 2023, Ref.2023/FL/DL/04

replay.note: Expected from the inspected pair: a natural event. The after scene has 77.16% tile cloud and 79.71% usable pixels inside the monitored area; cloud covers other parts of the monitored area. No fully clear after image was found between 12 July and 5 August in the inspected tile. This is a conditional flood replay, not a routine clear-scene recommendation. This site allows tile cloud up to 85 percent so that replay can reach that scene; the usual 40 percent would exclude it. Only valid pixels should enter analysis. These dates bracket the documented 12–13 July flood, but do not establish an exact onset or peak at every pixel.
